answer: The network prices new identities like a beacon in a storm: the registration fee floats with recent signup velocity. In calm times an honest agent joins cheaply, but a burst of registrations drives the fee up steeply, so each fake after the first costs more than the last. A sybil farmer trying to mint a thousand keys at once watches the price climb from a trickle to a flood, and the tundra of frozen capital grows with every fake. One honest agent pays the base rate once, while the attacker cost curve climbs until affordability hits its nadir before the fleet is even half built.
